title: Reused same-ID browser profile can invalidate intended artifact attribution
surface: Native extension test setup and runtime evidence
reproduction: Copy the established isolated frozen173 admin profile into a new owned profile.
Launch Chrome for Testing with the intended imported175 extension directory while the profile already registers the same extension ID at frozen173.
Observe Prepare/Snapshot and hash the intended175 directory without reading the actual loaded extension folder.
The observed dataset toast matches frozen173 and is absent from the intended175 bundle, exposing invalid artifact attribution.
expected: A test establishes actual active profile and loaded extension folder/version against the receipt before assigning results to a source revision. Same-ID registration cannot silently substitute another artifact.
actual: Prepare/Snapshot observations were attributed to175 from extension ID and intended-directory hash, while the base profile registers173 and the observed toast identifies its stale bundle. Earlier admin Site access had distinctive new UI but lacked exact loaded-path proof.
severity: S2: invalid release confidence and misleading defect attribution
priority: P1: repair evidence setup before further admin acceptance
